title: False review-remediation stall: turn counter accumulates across review cycles
description:
`progressTracker.reviewRemediationTurns` (internal/core/progress.go) counts turns spent with `fixPending` after a failed independent review, but it is only reset by `resetStall` (an escalation) and when `markReviewRejected` first enters remediation. It never resets when a fix lands or when a later review rejects the next diff, so turns accumulate across every review cycle in a run.

Once the total reaches 8, `reviewRemediationReason` reports "agent spent eight turns after a failed independent review without fixing anything" and the escalation ladder climbs, even though the agent fixed each finding.

Observed in session ee571636 (2026-10-04, adding five Ramp models to the catalog): four reviews each rejected the change for a distinct real bug and the agent fixed each one, yet false escalations fired at 16:07:57 (rung 1, nudge telling it to take a "materially different approach") and 16:14:31 (rung 2, forced model switch). Two more false trips would compact/restate and then pause the run to ask the person.

Fix: reset `reviewRemediationTurns` in `markReviewRejected` on every rejection, so it measures turns since the latest rejection without an edit. Add a test covering several reject→fix cycles that each take a few turns.
